text.p: Aetna Inc. said Friday that its profits fell more than 40 percent in the third quarter as it continued to transform itself from a property-casualty insurer into a managed health care provider.
The company said net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 fell to $122.4 million, or 77 cents a share, from $212.1 million, or $1.86 a share.
However, Aetna also said its revenues expanded to $4.15 billion from $3.19 billion as premiums grew to $2.69 billion from $1.83 billion.
The company's stock shot up $2.75 to $62.875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Aetna said the third-quarter results included the earnings of U.S. Healthcare Inc., which it acquired on July 19. The year-ago results included $99.5 million in earnings from the company's property-casualty business, which it sold to Travelers Group in April.
The company said its total health membership declined in the third quarter with the loss of a large contract, but premiums grew after its acquisition of U.S. Healthcare.
It said membership fell to 14.2 million from 14.3 million due to the loss of a contract covering 700,000 members.
Premiums, however, grew 54 percent to $2.3 billion from $1.5 billion, reflecting the addition of U.S. Healthcare, the company said

Aetna said its Aetna U.S. Healthcare unit, which provides managed care, indemnity and group insurance products, had operating earnings of $93.5 million, compared with $71.9 million a year ago, when results were from only Aetna health plans.

Operating earnings for Aetna Retirement Services, which markets life insurance, retirement and investment products, expanded 21 percent to $49.3 million from $40.7 million. The total for the latest period excludes a $31.8 million restructuring charge.
Aetna said operating earnings for Aetna International, which sells life insurance and financial products in emerging markets, grew to $27.2 million from $24.0 million.
